Directions for Questions 96 to 100:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
"True education is far more than the simple accumulation of academic diplomas or rote data. It represents the
harmonious development of intellectual curiosity, moral rectitude, and civic duty. An educated mind learns to
question entrenched prejudices, dissect illogical dogmas, and approach societal problems with empathy and
scientific temper. When citizens are genuinely educated, democratic discourse is enriched, communal friction
diminishes, and innovation flourishes organically. Investment in accessible, high-quality primary and secondary
schooling is thus the most enduring safeguard for national vitality and social cohesion."
questions.questionText: According to the author, what constitutes true education?
options: Harmonious development of intellectual curiosity, moral rectitude, and civic duty
Solely the accumulation of degrees and diplomas
Securing commercial employment at any cost
